1: //! # UNUSED_ENGINE: Unused Constructions
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "UNUSED_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Unused Constructions"
6: //! category = "unused-constructions"
7: //! severity = "warning"
8: //! fix = false
9: //! icon = "lucide/trash-2"
10: //! slug = "unused"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects unused variables, functions, methods, and dead code in MATLAB
16: //! files. A single file-level engine (`UnusedEngine`) builds a symbol table
17: //! and runs unreachability analysis, then cross-references every definition
18: //! against its usages to identify dead code. It covers 17 checks from
19: //! MATLAB's "Unused Constructions" category; each diagnostic carries the
20: //! specific check ID (e.g. `NASGU`, `UNRCH`, `MSNU`).
21: //!
22: //! ## Check IDs
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
25: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: //! | NASGU | warning | no | Value assigned to variable might be unused. |
27: //! | NUSED | warning | no | Global or persistent variable might be unused or unset in this function or script. |
28: //! | NOEFF | warning | no | The operation or expression VAR_OPERATOR has no evident effect. |
29: //! | EQEFF | warning | no | To assign values to variables, use =. The == operator compares equality of values. |
30: //! | ASGLU | warning | no | Value assigned to variable might be unused. Consider replacing the variable with ~ instead. |
31: //! | SETNU | warning | no | Variable is set, but might be unused. |
32: //! | PUSE | warning | no | Persistent variable might be unused. |
33: //! | PREALL | warning | no | The preallocated value assigned to variable might be unused. |
34: //! | INUSA | warning | no | Input argument might be unused after the function arguments block(s). |
35: //! | INUSD | warning | no | Input argument might be unused. Consider replacing the argument with ~ instead. |
36: //! | VANUS | info | no | Input argument 'varargin' might be unused. |
37: //! | DEFNU | warning | no | Function might be unused. |
38: //! | UNRCH | warning | no | This statement (and possibly following ones) cannot be reached. |
39: //! | MANU | warning | no | Input argument might be unused. Consider replacing the argument with ~, or make this method Static instead. |
40: //! | VUNUS | warning | no | VAR_OPERATOR produces a value that might be unused. |
41: //! | MSNU | warning | no | A Code Analyzer message was once suppressed here, but the message is no longer generated. |
42: //! | MSNE | info | no | No Code Analyzer check is found for this check ID. |
43: //!
44: //! ## Examples
45: //!
46: //! ### Incorrect
47: //!
48: //! ```matlab
49: //! function f()
50: //!     temp = compute();   % NASGU: assigned but never used
51: //!     x = 1;
52: //!     return;
53: //!     y = x;              % UNRCH: unreachable after return
54: //!     s.field = 1;        % MSNU: set but never read
55: //! end
56: //! ```
57: //!
58: //! ### Correct
59: //!
60: //! ```matlab
61: //! function f()
62: //!     x = compute();
63: //!     disp(x);
64: //!     s.field = x;
65: //!     disp(s.field);
66: //! end
67: //! ```

72: //! [lint.rules.UNUSED_ENGINE]
73: //! severity = "warning"
74: //! ignore_patterns = ["_*", "unused*"]
75: //! disabled_checks = ["VANUS"]
76: //! ```

156: /// File-level rule engine for detecting unused constructions.
157: ///
158: /// This rule performs its analysis in `check_file()` by building a symbol table
159: /// and running unreachability analysis, then cross-referencing definitions with

165: impl UnusedEngine {
166:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
167:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
168:         let rule_config: UnusedConfig = config.rule_params("UNUSED_ENGINE");
169:         Box::new(Self {
170:             config: rule_config,
171:         })
172:     }

174:     /// Check if a check ID is disabled in config.
175:     fn is_check_disabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
176:         self.config
177:             .disabled_checks
178:             .iter()
179:             .any(|d| d.eq_ignore_ascii_case(check_id))
180:     }

182:     /// Check if a variable name should be ignored based on configured patterns.
183:     fn should_ignore_name(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
184:         // Always ignore `_` and names starting with `~`.
185:         if name == "_" || name.starts_with('~') {
186:             return true;
187:         }
188:         // Always ignore MATLAB built-in specials.
189:         if ALWAYS_USED.contains(&name) {
190:             return true;
191:         }
192:         // Check configured patterns.
193:         self.config
194:             .ignore_patterns
195:             .iter()
196:             .any(|pat| matches_simple_glob(pat, name))
197:     }

199:     /// Run MSNU check: struct field set but never read.
200:     /// This is a heuristic check based on field_expression analysis.
201:     fn check_msnu(&self, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
202:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNU") {
203:             return;
204:         }
205: 
206:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
207:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
208: 
209:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
210:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
211:             ctx.source,
212:             &mut field_writes,
213:             &mut field_reads,
214:         );
215: 
216:         // Report fields that are written but never read.
217:         for write in &field_writes {
218:             let key = format!("{}.{}", write.object, write.field);
219:             if !field_reads.contains(&key) {
220:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
221:                     rule_id: "MSNU",
222:                     message: "A Code Analyzer message was once suppressed here, but the message is no longer generated.".to_string(),
223:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
224:                     byte_range: write.byte_range.clone(),
225:                     line: write.line,
226:                     column: write.column,
227:                     fix: None,
228:                 });
229:             }
230:         }
231:     }

233:     /// Run MSNE check: struct field doesn't exist (assigned but potential typo).
234:     /// Heuristic: if a struct has many fields and one is only written once with
235:     /// no reads, it may be a typo.
236:     fn check_msne(&self, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
237:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNE") {
238:             return;
239:         }
240: 
241:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
242:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
243: 
244:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
245:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
246:             ctx.source,
247:             &mut field_writes,
248:             &mut field_reads,
249:         );
250: 
251:         // Group writes by object name.
252:         let mut writes_by_object: HashMap<&str, Vec<&FieldAccess>> = HashMap::new();
253:         for write in &field_writes {
254:             writes_by_object
255:                 .entry(write.object.as_str())
256:                 .or_default()
257:                 .push(write);
258:         }
259: 
260:         // For each object with multiple fields written, check if any field
261:         // is written exactly once and never read — potential typo.
262:         for (object, writes) in &writes_by_object {
263:             if writes.len() < 2 {
264:                 continue;
265:             }
266: 
267:             let mut field_write_count: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
268:             for w in writes {
269:                 *field_write_count.entry(w.field.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
270:             }
271: 
272:             for w in writes {
273:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", object, w.field);
274:                 if field_write_count.get(w.field.as_str()) == Some(&1)
275:                     && !field_reads.contains(&key)
276:                 {
277:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
278:                         rule_id: "MSNE",
279:                         message: "No Code Analyzer check is found for this check ID.".to_string(),
280:                         severity: Severity::Info,
281:                         byte_range: w.byte_range.clone(),
282:                         line: w.line,
283:                         column: w.column,
284:                         fix: None,
285:                     });
286:                 }
287:             }
288:         }
289:     }

291:     /// Collect field accesses (both reads and writes) from the parse tree.
292:     fn collect_field_accesses(
293:         node: Node,
294:         source: &str,
295:         writes: &mut Vec<FieldAccess>,
296:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
297:     ) {
298:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
299:             // Check if LHS is a field_expression.
300:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
301:                 if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
302:                     if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(lhs, source) {
303:                         writes.push(access);
304:                     }
305:                 }
306:             }
307:             // Check RHS for field reads.
308:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
309:                 Self::collect_field_reads(rhs, source, reads);
310:             }
311:         } else if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
312:             // A field_expression not on the LHS of assignment is a read.
313:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
314:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
315:                 reads.insert(key);
316:             }
317:         }
318: 
319:         // Recurse into children (skip assignment children we already handled).
320:         if node.kind() != "assignment" {
321:             let count = node.child_count();
322:             for i in 0..count {
323:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
324:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
325:                 }
326:             }
327:         } else {
328:             // For assignments, recurse into children except LHS field_expression.
329:             let count = node.child_count();
330:             for i in 0..count {
331:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
332:                     if child.kind() == "field_expression" {
333:                         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
334:                             if lhs.id() == child.id() {
335:                                 continue;
336:                             }
337:                         }
338:                     }
339:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
340:                 }
341:             }
342:         }
343:     }

345:     /// Collect field reads from an expression subtree.
346:     fn collect_field_reads(node: Node, source: &str, reads: &mut HashSet<String>) {
347:         if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
348:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
349:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);

352:         }
353: 
354:         let count = node.child_count();
355:         for i in 0..count {
356:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {

436: /// Extract a `FieldAccess` from a `field_expression` node.
437: pub(crate) fn extract_field_access(node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<FieldAccess> {
438:     // field_expression has an object and a field child.
439:     let object_node = node.child(0)?;
440:     let field_node = node.child_by_field_name("field")?;
441: 
442:     // Only handle simple identifier objects (not chained field access).
443:     if object_node.kind() != "identifier" {
444:         return None;
445:     }
446: 
447:     let object = source[object_node.start_byte()..object_node.end_byte()].to_string();
448:     let field = source[field_node.start_byte()..field_node.end_byte()].to_string();
449:     let pos = node.start_position();
450: 
451:     Some(FieldAccess {
452:         object,
453:         field,
454:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
455:         line: pos.row + 1,
456:         column: pos.column + 1,
457:     })
458: }

460: /// Simple glob pattern matching supporting `*` (any sequence) and `?` (single char).
461: pub(crate) fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
462:     let pat: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
463:     let txt: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
464:     glob_match_recursive(&pat, &txt, 0, 0)
465: }
466: 
467: /// Recursive glob matching helper.
468: pub(crate) fn glob_match_recursive(pat: &[char], txt: &[char], pi: usize, ti: usize) -> bool {
469:     if pi == pat.len() {
470:         return ti == txt.len();
471:     }
472: 
473:     match pat[pi] {
474:         '*' => {
475:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.
476:             for i in ti..=txt.len() {
477:                 if glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, i) {
478:                     return true;
479:                 }
480:             }
481:             false
482:         }
483:         '?' => {
484:             // `?` matches exactly one character.

9:         let eqeff_disabled = self.is_check_disabled("EQEFF");

12:             return;
13:         }
14: 
15:         // Walk the tree looking for expression nodes at statement level.
16:         walk_for_no_effect(

26: // No-effect statement walker (free function to satisfy clippy)
27: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
28: 
29: /// Recursively walk tree to find statement-level expressions with no effect.
30: pub(crate) fn walk_for_no_effect(
31:     node: Node,
32:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
33:     noeff_disabled: bool,
34:     eqeff_disabled: bool,
35: ) {
36:     // Check if this node is at statement level (parent is block or source_file).
37:     let is_statement_level = node
38:         .parent()
39:         .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
40:         .unwrap_or(false);
41: 
42:     if is_statement_level {
43:         let kind = node.kind();
44: 
45:         // EQEFF: comparison operator at statement level.
46:         if !eqeff_disabled && kind == COMPARISON_NODE {
47:             let pos = node.start_position();
48:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
49:                 rule_id: "EQEFF",
50:                 message: "To assign values to variables, use =. The == operator compares equality of values.".to_string(),
51:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
52:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
53:                 line: pos.row + 1,
54:                 column: pos.column + 1,
55:                 fix: None,
56:             });
57:         }
58:         // NOEFF: other expression nodes at statement level that are not
59:         // assignments, function_calls, or commands.
60:         else if !noeff_disabled && NO_EFFECT_EXPR_NODES.contains(&kind) {
61:             let pos = node.start_position();
62:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
63:                 rule_id: "NOEFF",
64:                 message: "The operation or expression VAR_OPERATOR has no evident effect."
65:                     .to_string(),
66:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
67:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
68:                 line: pos.row + 1,
69:                 column: pos.column + 1,
70:                 fix: None,
71:             });
72:         }
73:     }
74: 
75:     // Recurse into children.
76:     let count = node.child_count();
77:     for i in 0..count {
78:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
79:             walk_for_no_effect(child, diagnostics, noeff_disabled, eqeff_disabled);
80:         }
81:     }
82: }

1: //! # Symbol Table — Per-scope variable definition and usage tracking
2: //!
3: //! This module provides a [`SymbolTable`] that maps out every variable definition
4: //! and usage across all scopes in a MATLAB source file. It is the foundation for
5: //! rules that need scope-aware analysis such as unused variables, undefined
6: //! variables, and shadowed variables.
7: //!
8: //! ## How it works
9: //!
10: //! [`SymbolTable::build`] performs a single depth-first traversal of the
11: //! tree-sitter parse tree. It maintains a scope stack: every time it enters a
12: //! `function_definition` or `lambda`, a new [`Scope`] is pushed. When the
13: //! traversal leaves that node, the scope is popped.
14: //!
15: //! For each identifier encountered, the builder inspects the parent node to
16: //! decide whether the identifier is a **definition** ([`VarDef`]) or a
17: //! **usage** ([`VarUse`]). Definitions include input/output arguments,
18: //! assignment left-hand sides, for-loop iterators, `global`/`persistent`
19: //! declarations, nested function names, and lambda parameters. Everything
20: //! else is a usage.
21: //!
22: //! ## Example
23: //!
24: //! ```ignore
25: //! use tree_sitter::Parser;
26: //! use mlt_rules::analysis::symbols::SymbolTable;
27: //!
28: //! let source = "function y = foo(x)\n    y = x + 1;\nend\n";
29: //! let mut parser = Parser::new();
30: //! parser.set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into()).unwrap();
31: //! let tree = parser.parse(source, None).unwrap();
32: //!
33: //! let table = SymbolTable::build(&tree, source);
34: //! assert_eq!(table.scopes.len(), 1);
35: //! assert!(table.root_scope().is_defined("x"));
36: //! assert!(table.root_scope().is_defined("y"));
37: //! ```
38: 
39: use std::collections::HashSet;
40: use tree_sitter::Tree;
41: 
42: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43: // Definition kinds
44: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45: 
46: /// The type of a variable definition.
47: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
48: pub enum DefKind {
49:     /// Function input argument.
50:     InputArg,
51:     /// Function output argument.
52:     OutputArg,
53:     /// Assignment left-hand side (`x = ...`).
54:     Assignment,
55:     /// For-loop iterator variable.
56:     ForIterator,
57:     /// Global declaration (`global x`).
58:     Global,
59:     /// Persistent declaration (`persistent x`).
60:     Persistent,
61:     /// Nested function name.
62:     NestedFunction,
63:     /// Anonymous function parameter.
64:     LambdaParam,
65: }
66: 
67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: // VarDef / VarUse
69: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70: 
71: /// A single variable definition occurrence.
72: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
73: pub struct VarDef {
74:     /// The variable name.
75:     pub name: String,
76:     /// How it was defined.
77:     pub kind: DefKind,
78:     /// Byte range in source.
79:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
80:     /// 1-indexed line number.
81:     pub line: usize,
82:     /// 1-indexed column number.
83:     pub column: usize,
84: }
85: 
86: /// A single variable usage (read) occurrence.
87: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
88: pub struct VarUse {
89:     /// The variable name.
90:     pub name: String,
91:     /// Byte range in source.
92:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
93:     /// 1-indexed line number.
94:     pub line: usize,
95:     /// 1-indexed column number.
96:     pub column: usize,
97: }
98: 
99: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100: // Scope
101: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102: 
103: /// The type of scope.
104: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
105: pub enum ScopeKind {
106:     /// File-level script scope (no enclosing function).
107:     Script,
108:     /// Main function (first `function_definition` in file).
109:     Function,
110:     /// Local function (subsequent `function_definition`s at file level).
111:     LocalFunction,
112:     /// Nested function (`function_definition` inside another function).
113:     NestedFunction,
114:     /// Method (`function_definition` inside a `methods` block in a class).
115:     Method,
116:     /// Anonymous function body.
117:     Lambda,
118: }
119: 
120: /// A scope representing a function, script, or lambda body.
121: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
122: pub struct Scope {
123:     /// The name of the function/method (empty string for scripts/lambdas).
124:     pub name: String,
125:     /// The kind of scope.
126:     pub kind: ScopeKind,
127:     /// Byte range of the entire scope node.
128:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
129:     /// 1-indexed line of scope start.
130:     pub line: usize,
131:     /// All variable definitions in this scope.
132:     pub defs: Vec<VarDef>,
133:     /// All variable usages (reads) in this scope.
134:     pub uses: Vec<VarUse>,
135:     /// Child scope indices (nested functions, lambdas).
136:     pub children: Vec<usize>,
137:     /// Parent scope index (`None` for top-level).
138:     pub parent: Option<usize>,
139: }
140: 
141: impl Scope {
142:     /// Get all definitions of a variable by name.
143:     pub fn defs_of(&self, name: &str) -> Vec<&VarDef> {
144:         self.defs.iter().filter(|d| d.name == name).collect()
145:     }
146: 
147:     /// Get all usages of a variable by name.
148:     pub fn uses_of(&self, name: &str) -> Vec<&VarUse> {
149:         self.uses.iter().filter(|u| u.name == name).collect()
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Get all unique defined variable names.
153:     pub fn defined_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
154:         let mut seen = HashSet::new();
155:         self.defs
156:             .iter()
157:             .filter_map(|d| {
158:                 if seen.insert(d.name.as_str()) {
159:                     Some(d.name.as_str())
160:                 } else {
161:                     None
162:                 }
163:             })
164:             .collect()
165:     }
166: 
167:     /// Get all unique used variable names.
168:     pub fn used_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
169:         let mut seen = HashSet::new();
170:         self.uses
171:             .iter()
172:             .filter_map(|u| {
173:                 if seen.insert(u.name.as_str()) {
174:                     Some(u.name.as_str())
175:                 } else {
176:                     None
177:                 }
178:             })
179:             .collect()
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Check if a variable is defined in this scope.
183:     pub fn is_defined(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
184:         self.defs.iter().any(|d| d.name == name)
185:     }
186: 
187:     /// Check if a variable is used in this scope.
188:     pub fn is_used(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
189:         self.uses.iter().any(|u| u.name == name)
190:     }
191: }
192: 
193: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
194: // SymbolTable
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: 
197: /// The complete symbol table for a file.
198: ///
199: /// Contains all scopes (functions, scripts, lambdas) in the file, each with
200: /// their own definitions and usages. Scopes are stored in a flat `Vec` and
201: /// reference each other by index via [`Scope::children`] and [`Scope::parent`].
202: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
203: pub struct SymbolTable {
204:     /// All scopes in the file, indexed by position in this vec.
205:     pub scopes: Vec<Scope>,
206: }
207: 
208: impl SymbolTable {
209:     /// Get the root/file-level scope (index 0).
210:     pub fn root_scope(&self) -> &Scope {
211:         &self.scopes[0]
212:     }
213: 
214:     /// Get all function-level scopes (excluding lambdas and the root script scope).
215:     pub fn function_scopes(&self) -> Vec<&Scope> {
216:         self.scopes
217:             .iter()
218:             .filter(|s| {
219:                 matches!(
220:                     s.kind,
221:                     ScopeKind::Function
222:                         | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
223:                         | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
224:                         | ScopeKind::Method
225:                 )
226:             })
227:             .collect()
228:     }
229: 
230:     /// Find the innermost scope containing a given byte offset.
231:     ///
232:     /// Searches all scopes and returns the smallest (innermost) one whose
233:     /// byte range contains `byte_offset`.
234:     pub fn scope_at(&self, byte_offset: usize) -> Option<&Scope> {
235:         self.scopes
236:             .iter()
237:             .filter(|s| s.byte_range.contains(&byte_offset))
238:             .min_by_key(|s| s.byte_range.end - s.byte_range.start)
239:     }
240: 
241:     /// Build a symbol table from a parsed tree and source text.
242:     ///
243:     /// Performs a single DFS traversal of the tree-sitter parse tree, tracking
244:     /// scopes and collecting variable definitions and usages.
245:     pub fn build(tree: &Tree, source: &str) -> Self {
246:         let mut builder = Builder {
247:             source,
248:             scopes: Vec::new(),
249:             scope_stack: Vec::new(),
250:             first_file_function_seen: false,
251:         };
252:         builder.run(tree);
253:         SymbolTable {
254:             scopes: builder.scopes,
255:         }
256:     }
257: }
258: 
259: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
260: // Builder (private)
261: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
262: 
263: /// Internal builder that drives the DFS traversal and populates scopes.
264: struct Builder<'a> {
265:     source: &'a str,
266:     scopes: Vec<Scope>,
267:     /// Stack of scope indices: the last element is the "current" scope.
268:     scope_stack: Vec<usize>,
269:     /// Whether we have seen the first file-level `function_definition`.
270:     first_file_function_seen: bool,
271: }
272: 
273: impl<'a> Builder<'a> {
274:     // -- scope helpers ------------------------------------------------------
275: 
276:     /// Push a new scope and return its index.
277:     fn push_scope(&mut self, scope: Scope) -> usize {
278:         let idx = self.scopes.len();
279:         // Wire up parent ↔ child.
280:         let parent = self.scope_stack.last().copied();
281:         let mut scope = scope;
282:         scope.parent = parent;
283:         if let Some(p) = parent {
284:             self.scopes[p].children.push(idx);
285:         }
286:         self.scopes.push(scope);
287:         self.scope_stack.push(idx);
288:         idx
289:     }
290: 
291:     /// Pop the current scope off the stack.
292:     fn pop_scope(&mut self) {
293:         self.scope_stack.pop();
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Index of the current scope, if any.
297:     fn current_scope(&self) -> Option<usize> {
298:         self.scope_stack.last().copied()
299:     }
300: 
301:     /// Add a definition to the current scope.
302:     fn add_def(&mut self, def: VarDef) {
303:         if let Some(idx) = self.current_scope() {
304:             self.scopes[idx].defs.push(def);
305:         }
306:     }
307: 
308:     /// Add a usage to the current scope.
309:     fn add_use(&mut self, var_use: VarUse) {
310:         if let Some(idx) = self.current_scope() {
311:             self.scopes[idx].uses.push(var_use);
312:         }
313:     }
314: 
315:     /// Extract the text of a node from source.
316:     fn node_text(&self, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> &'a str {
317:         &self.source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
318:     }
319: 
320:     // -- main entry ---------------------------------------------------------
321: 
322:     /// Run the full build.
323:     fn run(&mut self, tree: &'a Tree) {
324:         let root = tree.root_node();
325: 
326:         // Determine if this is a script or function file.
327:         // A function file starts with a `function_definition` as the first
328:         // meaningful child of `source_file`. Otherwise it's a script.
329:         let is_function_file = Self::first_meaningful_child_is_function(&root);
330: 
331:         if !is_function_file {
332:             // Script file: the entire file is one Script scope.
333:             let pos = root.start_position();
334:             self.push_scope(Scope {
335:                 name: String::new(),
336:                 kind: ScopeKind::Script,
337:                 byte_range: root.start_byte()..root.end_byte(),
338:                 line: pos.row + 1,
339:                 defs: Vec::new(),
340:                 uses: Vec::new(),
341:                 children: Vec::new(),
342:                 parent: None,
343:             });
344:         }
345: 
346:         // Walk children of source_file.
347:         self.visit_children(root);
348: 
349:         // If this was a function file and we never pushed a scope, that
350:         // shouldn't happen, but guard against it.
351:         if self.scopes.is_empty() {
352:             let pos = root.start_position();
353:             self.push_scope(Scope {
354:                 name: String::new(),
355:                 kind: ScopeKind::Script,
356:                 byte_range: root.start_byte()..root.end_byte(),
357:                 line: pos.row + 1,
358:                 defs: Vec::new(),
359:                 uses: Vec::new(),
360:                 children: Vec::new(),
361:                 parent: None,
362:             });
363:         }
364:     }
365: 
366:     /// Check if the first non-comment child of `source_file` is a function.
367:     fn first_meaningful_child_is_function(root: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
368:         let count = root.child_count();
369:         for i in 0..count {
370:             if let Some(child) = root.child(i) {
371:                 match child.kind() {
372:                     "comment" | "line_continuation" => continue,
373:                     "function_definition" => return true,
374:                     _ => return false,
375:                 }
376:             }
377:         }
378:         false
379:     }
380: 
381:     // -- recursive visitor --------------------------------------------------
382: 
383:     /// Visit all children of a node, dispatching each to the appropriate handler.
384:     fn visit_children(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
385:         let count = node.child_count();
386:         for i in 0..count {
387:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
388:                 self.visit_node(child);
389:             }
390:         }
391:     }
392: 
393:     /// Dispatch a single node.
394:     fn visit_node(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
395:         match node.kind() {
396:             "function_definition" => self.visit_function_definition(node),
397:             "lambda" => self.visit_lambda(node),
398:             "assignment" => self.visit_assignment(node),
399:             "for_statement" => self.visit_for_statement(node),
400:             "global_operator" => self.visit_global_persistent(node, DefKind::Global),
401:             "persistent_operator" => self.visit_global_persistent(node, DefKind::Persistent),
402:             "identifier" => self.visit_identifier(node),
403:             // For all other nodes, just recurse into children.
404:             _ => self.visit_children(node),
405:         }
406:     }
407: 
408:     // -- function_definition ------------------------------------------------
409: 
410:     /// Visit a `function_definition` node.
411:     ///
412:     /// Creates a new scope, extracts input/output args, then recurses into
413:     /// the function body. Nested functions and methods are distinguished by
414:     /// the current scope stack depth and parent node context.
415:     fn visit_function_definition(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
416:         let pos = node.start_position();
417: 
418:         // Extract function name.
419:         let func_name = node
420:             .child_by_field_name("name")
421:             .map(|n| self.node_text(n).to_string())
422:             .unwrap_or_default();
423: 
424:         // Determine scope kind.
425:         let scope_kind = self.classify_function_scope(node);
426: 
427:         // If this is a nested function, register its name as a def in the
428:         // parent scope (so the parent can "call" it).
429:         if scope_kind == ScopeKind::NestedFunction {
430:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
431:                 let name_pos = name_node.start_position();
432:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
433:                     name: func_name.clone(),
434:                     kind: DefKind::NestedFunction,
435:                     byte_range: name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte(),
436:                     line: name_pos.row + 1,
437:                     column: name_pos.column + 1,
438:                 });
439:             }
440:         }
441: 
442:         // Push new scope.
443:         self.push_scope(Scope {
444:             name: func_name,
445:             kind: scope_kind,
446:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
447:             line: pos.row + 1,
448:             defs: Vec::new(),
449:             uses: Vec::new(),
450:             children: Vec::new(),
451:             parent: None, // set by push_scope
452:         });
453: 
454:         // Extract output arguments.
455:         self.extract_function_outputs(node);
456: 
457:         // Extract input arguments.
458:         self.extract_function_inputs(node);
459: 
460:         // Recurse into the function body (all children except the ones we
461:         // already handled).
462:         let count = node.child_count();
463:         for i in 0..count {
464:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
465:                 let kind = child.kind();
466:                 if kind == "function_arguments" || kind == "function_output" {
467:                     // Already handled above.
468:                     continue;
469:                 }
470:                 if kind == "identifier" {
471:                     // Skip the function name identifier (it's the `name` field).
472:                     if node
473:                         .child_by_field_name("name")
474:                         .map(|n| n.id() == child.id())
475:                         .unwrap_or(false)
476:                     {
477:                         continue;
478:                     }
479:                 }
480:                 self.visit_node(child);
481:             }
482:         }
483: 
484:         self.pop_scope();
485:     }

487:     /// Classify a `function_definition` based on its position in the tree.
488:     fn classify_function_scope(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> ScopeKind {
489:         // Check if we're inside a `methods` block.
490:         if Self::is_inside_methods_block(node) {
491:             return ScopeKind::Method;
492:         }
493: 
494:         // Check if we're inside another function scope.
495:         if self
496:             .current_scope()
497:             .map(|idx| {
498:                 matches!(
499:                     self.scopes[idx].kind,
500:                     ScopeKind::Function
501:                         | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
502:                         | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
503:                         | ScopeKind::Method
504:                 )
505:             })
506:             .unwrap_or(false)
507:         {
508:             return ScopeKind::NestedFunction;
509:         }
510: 
511:         // File-level function.
512:         if !self.first_file_function_seen {
513:             self.first_file_function_seen = true;
514:             ScopeKind::Function
515:         } else {
516:             ScopeKind::LocalFunction
517:         }
518:     }

520:     /// Check if a node is inside a `methods` block (by walking parents).
521:     fn is_inside_methods_block(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
522:         let mut current = node.parent();
523:         while let Some(p) = current {
524:             if p.kind() == "methods" {
525:                 return true;
526:             }
527:             // Stop at class_definition level — don't walk further up.
528:             if p.kind() == "class_definition" || p.kind() == "source_file" {
529:                 break;
530:             }
531:             current = p.parent();
532:         }
533:         false
534:     }

536:     /// Extract output arguments from `function_output`.
537:     fn extract_function_outputs(&mut self, func_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
538:         let Some(output_node) = func_node.child_by_field_name("output") else {
539:             // Also try iterating children for "function_output".
540:             let count = func_node.child_count();
541:             for i in 0..count {
542:                 if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
543:                     if child.kind() == "function_output" {
544:                         self.extract_output_identifiers(child);
545:                         return;
546:                     }
547:                 }
548:             }
549:             return;
550:         };
551:         self.extract_output_identifiers(output_node);
552:     }

554:     /// Recursively extract identifiers from an output node.
555:     fn extract_output_identifiers(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
556:         match node.kind() {
557:             "identifier" => {
558:                 let pos = node.start_position();
559:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
560:                     name: self.node_text(node).to_string(),
561:                     kind: DefKind::OutputArg,
562:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
563:                     line: pos.row + 1,
564:                     column: pos.column + 1,
565:                 });
566:             }
567:             "multioutput_variable" | "function_output" => {
568:                 let count = node.child_count();
569:                 for i in 0..count {
570:                     if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
571:                         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
572:                             let pos = child.start_position();
573:                             self.add_def(VarDef {
574:                                 name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
575:                                 kind: DefKind::OutputArg,
576:                                 byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
577:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
578:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
579:                             });
580:                         } else if child.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
581:                             self.extract_output_identifiers(child);
582:                         }
583:                         // Skip `ignored_argument` (~).
584:                     }
585:                 }
586:             }
587:             _ => {}
588:         }
589:     }

591:     /// Extract input arguments from `function_arguments`.
592:     fn extract_function_inputs(&mut self, func_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
593:         let count = func_node.child_count();
594:         for i in 0..count {
595:             if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
596:                 if child.kind() == "function_arguments" {
597:                     self.extract_input_identifiers(child);
598:                     return;
599:                 }
600:             }
601:         }
602:     }

604:     /// Extract identifiers from a `function_arguments` node.
605:     fn extract_input_identifiers(&mut self, args_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
606:         let count = args_node.child_count();
607:         for i in 0..count {
608:             if let Some(child) = args_node.child(i) {

611:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
612:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),

617:                     });

626:     /// Visit a `lambda` node (`@(x, y) expr`).
627:     ///
628:     /// Creates a Lambda scope, extracts parameters, then visits the body.
629:     fn visit_lambda(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
630:         let pos = node.start_position();
631: 
632:         self.push_scope(Scope {
633:             name: String::new(),
634:             kind: ScopeKind::Lambda,
635:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
636:             line: pos.row + 1,
637:             defs: Vec::new(),
638:             uses: Vec::new(),
639:             children: Vec::new(),
640:             parent: None, // set by push_scope
641:         });
642: 
643:         // Extract lambda parameters. In tree-sitter-matlab, the lambda's
644:         // arguments node contains the parameter identifiers.
645:         let count = node.child_count();
646:         for i in 0..count {
647:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
648:                 if child.kind() == "arguments" || child.kind() == "lambda_arguments" {
649:                     let arg_count = child.child_count();
650:                     for j in 0..arg_count {
651:                         if let Some(arg) = child.child(j) {
652:                             if arg.kind() == "identifier" {
653:                                 let arg_pos = arg.start_position();
654:                                 self.add_def(VarDef {
655:                                     name: self.node_text(arg).to_string(),
656:                                     kind: DefKind::LambdaParam,
657:                                     byte_range: arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte(),
658:                                     line: arg_pos.row + 1,
659:                                     column: arg_pos.column + 1,
660:                                 });
661:                             }
662:                         }
663:                     }
664:                 }
665:             }
666:         }
667: 
668:         // Visit body (all children that are not the arguments).
669:         for i in 0..count {
670:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
671:                 let kind = child.kind();
672:                 if kind == "arguments" || kind == "lambda_arguments" {
673:                     continue;
674:                 }
675:                 // Skip punctuation tokens like `@`, `(`, `)`.
676:                 if kind == "@" || kind == "(" || kind == ")" || kind == "," {
677:                     continue;
678:                 }
679:                 self.visit_node(child);
680:             }
681:         }
682: 
683:         self.pop_scope();
684:     }

686:     // -- assignment ---------------------------------------------------------
687: 
688:     /// Visit an `assignment` node.
689:     ///
690:     /// Extracts LHS identifiers as definitions, then visits the RHS as usages.
691:     fn visit_assignment(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
692:         // Process LHS: definitions.
693:         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
694:             self.extract_assignment_lhs(lhs);
695:         }
696: 
697:         // Process RHS: usages (just recurse normally).
698:         if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
699:             self.visit_node(rhs);
700:         }
701:     }
702: 
703:     /// Extract definitions from an assignment LHS.
704:     fn extract_assignment_lhs(&mut self, lhs: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
705:         match lhs.kind() {
706:             "identifier" => {
707:                 let pos = lhs.start_position();
708:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
709:                     name: self.node_text(lhs).to_string(),
710:                     kind: DefKind::Assignment,
711:                     byte_range: lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte(),
712:                     line: pos.row + 1,
713:                     column: pos.column + 1,
714:                 });
715:             }
716:             "multioutput_variable" => {
717:                 let count = lhs.child_count();
718:                 for i in 0..count {
719:                     if let Some(child) = lhs.child(i) {
720:                         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
721:                             let pos = child.start_position();
722:                             self.add_def(VarDef {
723:                                 name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
724:                                 kind: DefKind::Assignment,
725:                                 byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
726:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
727:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
728:                             });
729:                         }
730:                         // Skip `ignored_argument` (~) and punctuation.
731:                     }
732:                 }
733:             }
734:             "function_call" => {
735:                 // Indexed assignment: `A(i) = ...` or `obj.field = ...`.
736:                 // The name of the function_call is the variable being
737:                 // assigned into; we treat it as a usage (the variable must
738:                 // already exist). Arguments are usages too. Recurse normally.
739:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
740:             }
741:             "field_expression" => {
742:                 // `obj.field = ...` — `obj` is a usage.
743:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
744:             }
745:             "cell_index" => {
746:                 // `C{i} = ...` — treat like indexed assignment.
747:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
748:             }
749:             _ => {
750:                 // Unknown LHS shape — recurse for safety.
751:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
752:             }
753:         }
754:     }

756:     // -- for_statement ------------------------------------------------------
757: 
758:     /// Visit a `for_statement` node.
759:     ///
760:     /// Extracts the iterator variable as a definition, then visits the body.
761:     fn visit_for_statement(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
762:         // The for statement has an `iterator` child that contains the loop
763:         // variable and the range expression.
764:         let count = node.child_count();
765:         for i in 0..count {
766:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
767:                 if child.kind() == "iterator" {
768:                     self.visit_iterator(child);
769:                 } else {
770:                     self.visit_node(child);
771:                 }
772:             }
773:         }
774:     }
775: 
776:     /// Visit an `iterator` node inside a for-statement.
777:     ///
778:     /// The first identifier child is the loop variable (definition).
779:     /// Everything else (the range expression) is visited for usages.
780:     fn visit_iterator(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
781:         let mut found_var = false;
782:         let count = node.child_count();
783:         for i in 0..count {
784:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
785:                 if !found_var && child.kind() == "identifier" {
786:                     // This is the loop variable.
787:                     let pos = child.start_position();
788:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
789:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
790:                         kind: DefKind::ForIterator,
791:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
792:                         line: pos.row + 1,
793:                         column: pos.column + 1,
794:                     });
795:                     found_var = true;
796:                 } else if child.kind() == "=" {
797:                     // Skip the `=` token.
798:                     continue;
799:                 } else {
800:                     // Range expression — visit for usages.
801:                     self.visit_node(child);
802:                 }
803:             }
804:         }
805:     }

810:     ///
811:     /// Each child identifier is a declaration.
812:     fn visit_global_persistent(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, kind: DefKind) {
813:         let count = node.child_count();
814:         for i in 0..count {
815:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
816:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
817:                     let pos = child.start_position();
818:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
819:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
820:                         kind,
821:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
822:                         line: pos.row + 1,
823:                         column: pos.column + 1,
824:                     });
825:                 }
826:             }
827:         }
828:     }

830:     // -- identifier (the tricky one) ----------------------------------------
831: 
832:     /// Visit a bare `identifier` node.
833:     ///
834:     /// Determines from parent context whether this identifier is a definition
835:     /// (already captured elsewhere), a function/field name (skip), or a
836:     /// genuine variable usage.
837:     fn visit_identifier(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
838:         let Some(parent) = node.parent() else {
839:             // Orphan identifier — treat as usage to be safe.
840:             self.record_use(node);
841:             return;
842:         };
843: 
844:         match parent.kind() {
845:             // Already handled by visit_assignment.
846:             "assignment" => {
847:                 if parent
848:                     .child_by_field_name("left")
849:                     .map(|l| l.id() == node.id())
850:                     .unwrap_or(false)
851:                 {
852:                     // This is the simple LHS identifier — already captured.
853:                     return;
854:                 }
855:                 // Otherwise it's on the RHS — it's a usage.
856:                 self.record_use(node);
857:             }
858: 
859:             // Already handled by extract_assignment_lhs.
860:             "multioutput_variable" => {
861:                 // Check if the multioutput_variable is the LHS of an assignment.
862:                 if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
863:                     if grandparent.kind() == "assignment"
864:                         && grandparent
865:                             .child_by_field_name("left")
866:                             .map(|l| l.id() == parent.id())
867:                             .unwrap_or(false)
868:                     {
869:                         // Already captured as assignment def.
870:                         return;
871:                     }
872:                     // multioutput_variable in function_output context.
873:                     if grandparent.kind() == "function_output" {
874:                         return;
875:                     }
876:                 }
877:                 self.record_use(node);
878:             }
879: 
880:             // Function definition name — skip (not a variable usage).
881:             "function_definition" => {
882:                 if parent
883:                     .child_by_field_name("name")
884:                     .map(|n| n.id() == node.id())
885:                     .unwrap_or(false)
886:                 {
887:                     return;
888:                 }
889:                 // Could be a child that's not the name — e.g., part of
890:                 // the body that was somehow an identifier child. Visit as use.
891:                 self.record_use(node);
892:             }
893: 
894:             // function_arguments / function_output — already handled.
895:             "function_arguments" | "function_output" => {
896:                 // Already captured as InputArg / OutputArg.
897:             }
898: 
899:             // global/persistent — already handled.
900:             "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => {
901:                 // Already captured as Global / Persistent.
902:             }
903: 
904:             // For-loop iterator — already handled.
905:             "iterator" => {
906:                 // Already captured as ForIterator. But the range expression
907:                 // identifiers also have parent `iterator`. We need to check if
908:                 // this is the first identifier (the loop var) or a later one.
909:                 // The first identifier child of `iterator` is the loop var.
910:                 let first_ident = Self::first_identifier_child(parent);
911:                 if first_ident.map(|n| n.id() == node.id()).unwrap_or(false) {
912:                     // This is the loop variable — already captured.
913:                     return;
914:                 }
915:                 // Otherwise it's part of the range expression.
916:                 self.record_use(node);
917:             }
918: 
919:             // Lambda arguments — already handled.
920:             "arguments" | "lambda_arguments" => {
921:                 // Only skip if the parent's parent is a lambda.
922:                 if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
923:                     if grandparent.kind() == "lambda" {
924:                         return;
925:                     }
926:                 }
927:                 self.record_use(node);
928:             }
929: 
930:             // Function call name: count as usage (could be array indexing).
931:             "function_call" => {
932:                 // The `name` field of function_call should be counted as a
933:                 // usage because it could be array indexing (`A(i)`), where
934:                 // `A` must be defined.
935:                 self.record_use(node);
936:             }
937: 
938:             // Field expression: only the `object` part is a usage, not the
939:             // `field` part.
940:             "field_expression" => {
941:                 if parent
942:                     .child_by_field_name("field")
943:                     .map(|f| f.id() == node.id())
944:                     .unwrap_or(false)
945:                 {
946:                     // This is the field name (e.g., `field` in `obj.field`).
947:                     // Not a standalone variable usage.
948:                     return;
949:                 }
950:                 // This is the object part — it's a usage.
951:                 self.record_use(node);
952:             }
953: 
954:             // Class definition name — skip.
955:             "class_definition" => {
956:                 if parent
957:                     .child_by_field_name("name")
958:                     .map(|n| n.id() == node.id())
959:                     .unwrap_or(false)
960:                 {
961:                     return;
962:                 }
963:                 self.record_use(node);
964:             }
965: 
966:             // Default: it's a variable usage.
967:             _ => {
968:                 self.record_use(node);
969:             }
970:         }
971:     }
972: 
973:     /// Find the first `identifier` child of a node.
974:     fn first_identifier_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
975:         let count = node.child_count();
976:         for i in 0..count {
977:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
978:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
979:                     return Some(child);
980:                 }
981:             }
982:         }
983:         None
984:     }
985: 
986:     /// Record a variable usage at the given identifier node.
987:     fn record_use(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node) {
988:         let pos = node.start_position();
989:         self.add_use(VarUse {
990:             name: self.node_text(node).to_string(),
991:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
992:             line: pos.row + 1,
993:             column: pos.column + 1,
994:         });
995:     }
996: }

1: //! # Control Flow Analysis — Reachability and Definite-Assignment Tracking
2: //!
3: //! This module provides two core analyses for MATLAB source files:
4: //!
5: //! 1. **Unreachable code detection** ([`find_unreachable`]) — identifies statements
6: //!    that follow `return`, `break`, or `continue` within the same block and can
7: //!    therefore never execute.
8: //!
9: //! 2. **Definite-assignment analysis** ([`analyze_definite_assignment`]) — determines
10: //!    which variables are guaranteed to have been assigned before a given point in
11: //!    a function, and which variable uses might reference unset variables. This is
12: //!    the foundation for "unset variables" lint rules.
13: //!
14: //! Both analyses operate on tree-sitter parse trees produced by `tree-sitter-matlab`.
15: //!
16: //! ## Unreachable code example
17: //!
18: //! ```ignore
19: //! function foo()
20: //!     return;
21: //!     x = 1;   % ← unreachable
22: //!     disp(x); % ← unreachable
23: //! end
24: //! ```
25: //!
26: //! ## Definite-assignment example
27: //!
28: //! ```ignore
29: //! function y = foo(x)
30: //!     if x > 0
31: //!         z = 1;
32: //!     end
33: //!     y = z;  % ← z is possibly unset (no else branch)
34: //! end
35: //! ```
36: //!
37: //! ## Usage
38: //!
39: //! ```ignore
40: //! use tree_sitter::Parser;
41: //! use mlt_rules::analysis::control_flow::{find_unreachable, analyze_definite_assignment};
42: //!
43: //! let source = "function foo()\n    return;\n    x = 1;\nend\n";
44: //! let mut parser = Parser::new();
45: //! parser.set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into()).unwrap();
46: //! let tree = parser.parse(source, None).unwrap();
47: //!
48: //! let unreachable = find_unreachable(&tree, source);
49: //! assert_eq!(unreachable.len(), 1);
50: //!
51: //! // For definite-assignment, pass the function_definition node:
52: //! let root = tree.root_node();
53: //! let func_node = root.child(0).unwrap();
54: //! let da = analyze_definite_assignment(func_node, source);
55: //! ```
56: 
57: use std::collections::HashSet;
58: use tree_sitter::{Node, Tree};
59: 
60: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
61: // Unreachable code types
62: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
63: 
64: /// A span of code that can never be reached because it follows a
65: /// `return`, `break`, or `continue` statement in the same block.
66: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
67: pub struct UnreachableSpan {
68:     /// Byte range of the unreachable code.
69:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
70:     /// 1-indexed line where unreachable code starts.
71:     pub line: usize,
72:     /// 1-indexed column where unreachable code starts.
73:     pub column: usize,
74:     /// The statement kind that causes unreachability (`"return"`, `"break"`, or `"continue"`).
75:     pub cause: &'static str,
76: }
77: 
78: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
79: // Definite-assignment types
80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81: 
82: /// Result of definite-assignment analysis for a single function scope.
83: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
84: pub struct DefiniteAssignment {
85:     /// Variables that are definitely assigned at every path to the end of the function.
86:     pub definitely_assigned: HashSet<String>,
87:     /// Variables that are possibly unset (assigned on some paths but not all)
88:     /// at the point where they are first used.
89:     pub possibly_unset: Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
90: }
91: 
92: /// A variable that might not be assigned before its use.
93: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
94: pub struct PossiblyUnsetVar {
95:     /// Variable name.
96:     pub name: String,
97:     /// Byte range of the use site.
98:     pub use_byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
99:     /// 1-indexed line of the use.
100:     pub use_line: usize,
101:     /// 1-indexed column of the use.
102:     pub use_column: usize,
103: }
104: 
105: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
106: // Helpers
107: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
108: 
109: /// Extract the source text covered by a node.
110: fn node_text<'a>(node: Node, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
111:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
112: }
113: 
114: /// Returns the termination cause string for a terminating statement node kind.
115: fn termination_cause(kind: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
116:     match kind {
117:         "return_statement" => Some("return"),
118:         "break_statement" => Some("break"),
119:         "continue_statement" => Some("continue"),
120:         _ => None,
121:     }
122: }
123: 
124: /// Iterate the named children of a node.
125: fn named_children(node: Node) -> Vec<Node> {
126:     let mut children = Vec::new();
127:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
128:     for child in node.named_children(&mut cursor) {
129:         children.push(child);
130:     }
131:     children
132: }

134: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
135: // 1. Unreachable code detection
136: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
137: 
138: /// Find all spans of unreachable code in a file.
139: ///
140: /// Walks every `block` node in the parse tree via DFS. Within each block,
141: /// when a `return_statement`, `break_statement`, or `continue_statement` is
142: /// encountered, all subsequent named sibling statements in that block are
143: /// collected as unreachable.
144: pub fn find_unreachable(tree: &Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<UnreachableSpan> {
145:     let mut spans = Vec::new();
146:     collect_unreachable_dfs(tree.root_node(), source, &mut spans);
147:     spans
148: }
149: 
150: /// DFS helper that visits every node and, for `block` nodes, checks for
151: /// unreachable code after terminating statements.
152: fn collect_unreachable_dfs(node: Node, source: &str, spans: &mut Vec<UnreachableSpan>) {
153:     if node.kind() == "block" {
154:         check_block_unreachable(node, source, spans);
155:     }
156: 
157:     // Recurse into all named children regardless — blocks inside if/for/etc.
158:     // are children of those compound statements, not of the outer block.
159:     let children = named_children(node);
160:     for child in children {
161:         collect_unreachable_dfs(child, source, spans);
162:     }
163: }
164: 
165: /// For a single `block` node, find the first terminating statement and mark
166: /// all subsequent named siblings as unreachable.
167: fn check_block_unreachable(block: Node, source: &str, spans: &mut Vec<UnreachableSpan>) {
168:     let children = named_children(block);
169:     let mut terminator_found: Option<&'static str> = None;
170: 
171:     for child in &children {
172:         if let Some(cause) = terminator_found {
173:             // Skip comment nodes — they are not "code".
174:             if child.kind() == "comment" {
175:                 continue;
176:             }
177:             let pos = child.start_position();
178:             spans.push(UnreachableSpan {
179:                 byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
180:                 line: pos.row + 1,
181:                 column: pos.column + 1,
182:                 cause,
183:             });
184:         } else if let Some(cause) = termination_cause(child.kind()) {
185:             terminator_found = Some(cause);
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:     let _ = source; // used implicitly through node byte ranges
190: }
191: 
192: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
193: // 2. Block termination check
194: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
195: 
196: /// Check if a `block` node unconditionally terminates (all paths through it
197: /// reach a `return`, `break`, or `continue` statement).
198: ///
199: /// A block terminates if:
200: /// - It directly contains a `return_statement`, `break_statement`, or
201: ///   `continue_statement` at the top level, OR
202: /// - Its last named statement is an `if_statement` that has an `else_clause`
203: ///   and ALL branches (if, elseif*, else) terminate, OR
204: /// - Its last named statement is a `switch_statement` that has an
205: ///   `otherwise_clause` and ALL cases plus otherwise terminate.
206: pub fn block_terminates(block_node: Node) -> bool {
207:     let children = named_children(block_node);
208: 
209:     for child in &children {
210:         // Direct terminator at top level → block terminates.
211:         if termination_cause(child.kind()).is_some() {
212:             return true;
213:         }
214:     }
215: 
216:     // Check the last named statement for compound termination.
217:     if let Some(last) = children.last() {
218:         match last.kind() {
219:             "if_statement" => return if_terminates(*last),
220:             "switch_statement" => return switch_terminates(*last),
221:             _ => {}
222:         }
223:     }
224: 
225:     false
226: }
227: 
228: /// Check if an `if_statement` unconditionally terminates.
229: ///
230: /// Requires an `else_clause`, and every branch body must terminate.
231: fn if_terminates(if_node: Node) -> bool {
232:     let mut has_else = false;
233:     let children = named_children(if_node);
234: 
235:     // The if body is the `block` child directly under the if_statement.
236:     // elseif_clause and else_clause are also named children.
237: 
238:     // Find the main if-body block.
239:     let mut if_body_terminates = false;
240:     for child in &children {
241:         if child.kind() == "block" {
242:             if_body_terminates = block_terminates(*child);
243:             break;
244:         }
245:     }
246: 
247:     if !if_body_terminates {
248:         return false;
249:     }
250: 
251:     for child in &children {
252:         match child.kind() {
253:             "elseif_clause" => {
254:                 // Each elseif has a block child.
255:                 let elseif_children = named_children(*child);
256:                 let body = elseif_children.iter().find(|c| c.kind() == "block");
257:                 match body {
258:                     Some(b) if block_terminates(*b) => {}
259:                     _ => return false,
260:                 }
261:             }
262:             "else_clause" => {
263:                 has_else = true;
264:                 let else_children = named_children(*child);
265:                 let body = else_children.iter().find(|c| c.kind() == "block");
266:                 match body {
267:                     Some(b) if block_terminates(*b) => {}
268:                     _ => return false,
269:                 }
270:             }
271:             _ => {}
272:         }
273:     }
274: 
275:     // Must have an else clause for complete coverage.
276:     has_else
277: }
278: 
279: /// Check if a `switch_statement` unconditionally terminates.
280: ///
281: /// Requires an `otherwise_clause`, and every case plus otherwise must terminate.
282: fn switch_terminates(switch_node: Node) -> bool {
283:     let mut has_otherwise = false;
284:     let children = named_children(switch_node);
285: 
286:     for child in &children {
287:         match child.kind() {
288:             "case_clause" => {
289:                 let case_children = named_children(*child);
290:                 let body = case_children.iter().find(|c| c.kind() == "block");
291:                 match body {
292:                     Some(b) if block_terminates(*b) => {}
293:                     _ => return false,
294:                 }
295:             }
296:             "otherwise_clause" => {
297:                 has_otherwise = true;
298:                 let ow_children = named_children(*child);
299:                 let body = ow_children.iter().find(|c| c.kind() == "block");
300:                 match body {
301:                     Some(b) if block_terminates(*b) => {}
302:                     _ => return false,
303:                 }
304:             }
305:             _ => {}
306:         }
307:     }
308: 
309:     has_otherwise
310: }

312: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
313: // 3. Definite-assignment analysis
314: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
315: 
316: /// Analyze definite assignment for a single function scope.
317: ///
318: /// `func_node` should be a `function_definition` node. The analysis:
319: /// 1. Collects input and output arguments as definitely assigned.
320: /// 2. Walks the function body, tracking which variables are definitely assigned.
321: /// 3. For each variable use, checks whether it is in the definitely-assigned set.
322: ///    If not (and it is not a known global/persistent), records it as possibly unset.
323: pub fn analyze_definite_assignment(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> DefiniteAssignment {
324:     let mut assigned: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
325:     let mut possibly_unset: Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar> = Vec::new();
326: 
327:     // Collect function input arguments as definitely assigned.
328:     collect_function_args(func_node, source, &mut assigned);
329: 
330:     // Find the function body block.
331:     let children = named_children(func_node);
332:     for child in &children {
333:         if child.kind() == "block" {
334:             walk_block(*child, source, &mut assigned, &mut possibly_unset);
335:             break;
336:         }
337:     }
338: 
339:     DefiniteAssignment {
340:         definitely_assigned: assigned,
341:         possibly_unset,
342:     }
343: }
344: 
345: /// Collect input and output argument names from a `function_definition` node
346: /// into the `assigned` set.
347: fn collect_function_args(func_node: Node, source: &str, assigned: &mut HashSet<String>) {
348:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
349:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
350:         match child.kind() {
351:             "function_arguments" => {
352:                 let mut inner = child.walk();
353:                 for param in child.children(&mut inner) {
354:                     if param.kind() == "identifier" {
355:                         assigned.insert(node_text(param, source).to_string());
356:                     }
357:                 }
358:             }
359:             "function_output" => {
360:                 collect_output_identifiers(child, source, assigned);
361:             }
362:             _ => {}
363:         }
364:     }
365: }
366: 
367: /// Recursively collect output identifiers (handles `multioutput_variable`).
368: fn collect_output_identifiers(node: Node, source: &str, assigned: &mut HashSet<String>) {
369:     match node.kind() {
370:         "identifier" => {
371:             assigned.insert(node_text(node, source).to_string());
372:         }
373:         "multioutput_variable" | "function_output" => {
374:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
375:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
376:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
377:                     assigned.insert(node_text(child, source).to_string());
378:                 } else if child.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
379:                     collect_output_identifiers(child, source, assigned);
380:                 }
381:             }
382:         }
383:         _ => {}
384:     }
385: }

387: /// Walk a `block` node, updating the definitely-assigned set and recording
388: /// possibly-unset variable uses.
389: fn walk_block(
390:     block: Node,
391:     source: &str,
392:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
393:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
394: ) {
395:     let children = named_children(block);
396: 
397:     for child in &children {
398:         walk_statement(*child, source, assigned, uses);
399:     }
400: }

402: /// Process a single statement node within a block.
403: fn walk_statement(
404:     node: Node,
405:     source: &str,
406:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
407:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
408: ) {
409:     match node.kind() {
410:         "assignment" => {
411:             // First, check the RHS for uses of possibly-unset variables.
412:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
413:                 collect_uses_in_expr(rhs, source, assigned, uses);
414:             }
415:             // Then add LHS variables to the assigned set.
416:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
417:                 collect_assignment_targets(lhs, source, assigned, uses);
418:             }
419:         }
420:         "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => {
421:             // Global/persistent declarations make the variables definitely assigned.
422:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
423:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
424:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
425:                     assigned.insert(node_text(child, source).to_string());
426:                 }
427:             }
428:         }
429:         "if_statement" => {
430:             walk_if_statement(node, source, assigned, uses);
431:         }
432:         "switch_statement" => {
433:             walk_switch_statement(node, source, assigned, uses);
434:         }
435:         "for_statement" => {
436:             walk_for_statement(node, source, assigned, uses);
437:         }
438:         "while_statement" => {
439:             walk_while_statement(node, source, assigned, uses);
440:         }
441:         "try_statement" => {
442:             walk_try_statement(node, source, assigned, uses);
443:         }
444:         "return_statement" | "break_statement" | "continue_statement" => {
445:             // No more reachable code in this block after a terminator.
446:             // The caller (walk_block) will still iterate remaining children,
447:             // but that is fine — unreachable code detection is handled
448:             // separately by find_unreachable(). For definite-assignment we
449:             // could stop early, but for simplicity we continue (it won't
450:             // produce false positives since no new uses will appear in
451:             // unreachable code that matters).
452:             //
453:             // However, we should signal the caller to stop processing.
454:             // We handle this by returning early from walk_block via a
455:             // special approach — but to keep walk_block simple, we just
456:             // let it continue. Unreachable statements won't add incorrect
457:             // "possibly unset" entries because the variables they reference
458:             // would also be unreachable. This is acceptable for now.
459:         }
460:         "function_call" | "command" => {
461:             // Check all arguments for uses of unset variables.
462:             collect_uses_in_expr(node, source, assigned, uses);
463:         }
464:         _ => {
465:             // For any other statement type, recursively look for variable uses.
466:             collect_uses_in_expr(node, source, assigned, uses);
467:         }
468:     }
469: }
