471: /// Walk an `if_statement`, handling branch merging.
472: ///
473: /// A variable is definitely assigned after the if/elseif/else chain only if
474: /// it is assigned in ALL branches AND there IS an else branch.
475: fn walk_if_statement(
476:     node: Node,
477:     source: &str,
478:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
479:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
480: ) {
481:     let children = named_children(node);
482: 
483:     // Check the condition for uses.
484:     for child in &children {
485:         if child.kind() == "condition" {
486:             collect_uses_in_expr(*child, source, assigned, uses);
487:             break;
488:         }
489:     }
490: 
491:     let mut branch_sets: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
492:     let mut has_else = false;
493: 
494:     // Walk the main if-body block.
495:     for child in &children {
496:         if child.kind() == "block" {
497:             let mut branch_assigned = assigned.clone();
498:             walk_block(*child, source, &mut branch_assigned, uses);
499:             branch_sets.push(branch_assigned);
500:             break;
501:         }
502:     }
503: 
504:     // Walk elseif clauses.
505:     for child in &children {
506:         if child.kind() == "elseif_clause" {
507:             let elseif_children = named_children(*child);
508: 
509:             // Check elseif condition for uses.
510:             for ec in &elseif_children {
511:                 if ec.kind() == "condition" {
512:                     collect_uses_in_expr(*ec, source, assigned, uses);
513:                     break;
514:                 }
515:             }
516: 
517:             // Walk elseif body.
518:             for ec in &elseif_children {
519:                 if ec.kind() == "block" {
520:                     let mut branch_assigned = assigned.clone();
521:                     walk_block(*ec, source, &mut branch_assigned, uses);
522:                     branch_sets.push(branch_assigned);
523:                     break;
524:                 }
525:             }
526:         }
527:     }
528: 
529:     // Walk else clause.
530:     for child in &children {
531:         if child.kind() == "else_clause" {
532:             has_else = true;
533:             let else_children = named_children(*child);
534:             for ec in &else_children {
535:                 if ec.kind() == "block" {
536:                     let mut branch_assigned = assigned.clone();
537:                     walk_block(*ec, source, &mut branch_assigned, uses);
538:                     branch_sets.push(branch_assigned);
539:                     break;
540:                 }
541:             }
542:         }
543:     }
544: 
545:     // Merge: if there is an else clause, intersect all branch sets.
546:     // Only variables assigned in ALL branches are definitely assigned.
547:     if has_else && !branch_sets.is_empty() {
548:         let intersection = intersect_sets(&branch_sets);
549:         for name in intersection {
550:             assigned.insert(name);
551:         }
552:     }
553:     // If there is no else clause, assignments inside branches are NOT
554:     // definitely assigned (the condition might be false).
555: }
556: 
557: /// Walk a `switch_statement`, handling branch merging.
558: ///
559: /// Similar to if: a variable is definitely assigned after the switch only
560: /// if it is assigned in ALL case clauses AND the otherwise clause.
561: fn walk_switch_statement(
562:     node: Node,
563:     source: &str,
564:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
565:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
566: ) {
567:     let children = named_children(node);
568: 
569:     // Check the switch expression for uses.
570:     for child in &children {
571:         if child.kind() == "condition" {
572:             collect_uses_in_expr(*child, source, assigned, uses);
573:             break;
574:         }
575:     }
576: 
577:     let mut branch_sets: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
578:     let mut has_otherwise = false;
579: 
580:     for child in &children {
581:         match child.kind() {
582:             "case_clause" => {
583:                 let case_children = named_children(*child);
584: 
585:                 // Check case expression for uses.
586:                 for cc in &case_children {
587:                     if cc.kind() == "condition" {
588:                         collect_uses_in_expr(*cc, source, assigned, uses);
589:                         break;
590:                     }
591:                 }
592: 
593:                 // Walk case body.
594:                 for cc in &case_children {
595:                     if cc.kind() == "block" {
596:                         let mut branch_assigned = assigned.clone();
597:                         walk_block(*cc, source, &mut branch_assigned, uses);
598:                         branch_sets.push(branch_assigned);
599:                         break;
600:                     }
601:                 }
602:             }
603:             "otherwise_clause" => {
604:                 has_otherwise = true;
605:                 let ow_children = named_children(*child);
606:                 for oc in &ow_children {
607:                     if oc.kind() == "block" {
608:                         let mut branch_assigned = assigned.clone();
609:                         walk_block(*oc, source, &mut branch_assigned, uses);
610:                         branch_sets.push(branch_assigned);
611:                         break;
612:                     }
613:                 }
614:             }
615:             _ => {}
616:         }
617:     }
618: 
619:     if has_otherwise && !branch_sets.is_empty() {
620:         let intersection = intersect_sets(&branch_sets);
621:         for name in intersection {
622:             assigned.insert(name);
623:         }
624:     }
625: }

627: /// Walk a `for_statement`.
628: ///
629: /// The loop iterator variable IS definitely assigned inside the loop body.
630: /// However, assignments inside the loop body are NOT definitely assigned
631: /// after the loop (the loop might not execute).
632: fn walk_for_statement(
633:     node: Node,
634:     source: &str,
635:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
636:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
637: ) {
638:     let children = named_children(node);
639: 
640:     // Find the iterator and extract the loop variable + range uses.
641:     let mut loop_var: Option<String> = None;
642:     for child in &children {
643:         if child.kind() == "iterator" {
644:             let mut found_var = false;
645:             let mut iter_cursor = child.walk();
646:             for ic in child.children(&mut iter_cursor) {
647:                 if !found_var && ic.kind() == "identifier" {
648:                     loop_var = Some(node_text(ic, source).to_string());
649:                     found_var = true;
650:                 } else if ic.kind() != "=" {
651:                     // Range expression — check for uses.
652:                     collect_uses_in_expr(ic, source, assigned, uses);
653:                 }
654:             }
655:             break;
656:         }
657:     }
658: 
659:     // Walk the loop body with a clone. The loop variable is added to the
660:     // cloned set so that it is considered assigned inside the body.
661:     for child in &children {
662:         if child.kind() == "block" {
663:             let mut body_assigned = assigned.clone();
664:             if let Some(ref var) = loop_var {
665:                 body_assigned.insert(var.clone());
666:             }
667:             walk_block(*child, source, &mut body_assigned, uses);
668:             // Do NOT merge body_assigned back — loop might not execute.
669:             break;
670:         }
671:     }
672: }
673: 
674: /// Walk a `while_statement`.
675: ///
676: /// Assignments inside the loop body are NOT definitely assigned after the
677: /// loop (the loop might not execute). The condition is checked for uses.
678: fn walk_while_statement(
679:     node: Node,
680:     source: &str,
681:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
682:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
683: ) {
684:     let children = named_children(node);
685: 
686:     // Check the condition for uses.
687:     for child in &children {
688:         if child.kind() == "condition" {
689:             collect_uses_in_expr(*child, source, assigned, uses);
690:             break;
691:         }
692:     }
693: 
694:     // Walk the body with a clone — do not merge back.
695:     for child in &children {
696:         if child.kind() == "block" {
697:             let mut body_assigned = assigned.clone();
698:             walk_block(*child, source, &mut body_assigned, uses);
699:             break;
700:         }
701:     }
702: }
703: 
704: /// Walk a `try_statement`.
705: ///
706: /// A variable assigned only in the try block is NOT definitely assigned
707: /// (the catch path might skip it). Only variables assigned in BOTH the
708: /// try body and the catch body are definitely assigned.
709: fn walk_try_statement(
710:     node: Node,
711:     source: &str,
712:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
713:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
714: ) {
715:     let children = named_children(node);
716: 
717:     let mut branch_sets: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
718: 
719:     // Walk the try body.
720:     for child in &children {
721:         if child.kind() == "block" {
722:             let mut try_assigned = assigned.clone();
723:             walk_block(*child, source, &mut try_assigned, uses);
724:             branch_sets.push(try_assigned);
725:             break;
726:         }
727:     }
728: 
729:     // Walk the catch clause.
730:     for child in &children {
731:         if child.kind() == "catch_clause" {
732:             let catch_children = named_children(*child);
733:             let mut catch_assigned = assigned.clone();
734: 
735:             // The catch identifier (if any) is definitely assigned inside catch.
736:             for cc in &catch_children {
737:                 if cc.kind() == "identifier" {
738:                     catch_assigned.insert(node_text(*cc, source).to_string());
739:                 }
740:             }
741: 
742:             for cc in &catch_children {
743:                 if cc.kind() == "block" {
744:                     walk_block(*cc, source, &mut catch_assigned, uses);
745:                     break;
746:                 }
747:             }
748: 
749:             branch_sets.push(catch_assigned);
750:         }
751:     }
752: 
753:     // Intersect: only variables assigned in both try and catch are definite.
754:     if branch_sets.len() >= 2 {
755:         let intersection = intersect_sets(&branch_sets);
756:         for name in intersection {
757:             assigned.insert(name);
758:         }
759:     }
760:     // If there is no catch clause, try-body assignments are still not
761:     // definitely assigned (an error could occur at any point).
762: }

764: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
765: // Expression-level use collection
766: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
767: 
768: /// Recursively walk an expression tree looking for `identifier` nodes that
769: /// represent variable uses. For each one, check if it is in the `assigned`
770: /// set. If not, record it as possibly unset.
771: ///
772: /// Skips identifiers that appear in non-use positions:
773: /// - Function name in `function_call` (could be a built-in or an external function).
774: /// - Field name in `field_expression` (not a standalone variable).
775: fn collect_uses_in_expr(
776:     node: Node,
777:     source: &str,
778:     assigned: &HashSet<String>,
779:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
780: ) {
781:     if node.kind() == "identifier" {
782:         if is_variable_use(node) {
783:             let name = node_text(node, source);
784:             if !assigned.contains(name) {
785:                 let pos = node.start_position();
786:                 uses.push(PossiblyUnsetVar {
787:                     name: name.to_string(),
788:                     use_byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
789:                     use_line: pos.row + 1,
790:                     use_column: pos.column + 1,
791:                 });
792:             }
793:         }
794:         return;
795:     }
796: 
797:     // Recurse into children.
798:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
799:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
800:         collect_uses_in_expr(child, source, assigned, uses);
801:     }
802: }
803: 
804: /// Determine if an `identifier` node represents a variable use (as opposed
805: /// to a function name or field name).
806: ///
807: /// Returns `false` for:
808: /// - The `name` child of a `function_call` (treated as a possible function name).
809: /// - The `field` child of a `field_expression`.
810: /// - Identifiers inside `function_arguments` or `function_output`.
811: fn is_variable_use(node: Node) -> bool {
812:     let Some(parent) = node.parent() else {
813:         return true;
814:     };
815: 
816:     match parent.kind() {
817:         "function_call" => {
818:             // The first named child (the function name) is not a variable use.
819:             // Arguments ARE variable uses — those are inside the argument
820:             // list, so the parent for those identifiers won't be function_call
821:             // directly (they'll be inside an `arguments` node or similar).
822:             //
823:             // Check if this identifier is the direct name of the function_call.
824:             // In tree-sitter-matlab, the function name is typically the first child
825:             // or accessible via a field. We check by position: if it's the first
826:             // named child, it's the function name.
827:             if let Some(first) = parent.child(0) {
828:                 if first.id() == node.id() {
829:                     return false;
830:                 }
831:             }
832:             true
833:         }
834:         "field_expression" => {
835:             // The field part (second identifier) is not a variable use.
836:             parent
837:                 .child_by_field_name("field")
838:                 .map(|f| f.id() != node.id())
839:                 .unwrap_or(true)
840:         }
841:         "function_arguments" | "function_output" | "function_definition" => false,
842:         _ => true,
843:     }
844: }
845: 
846: /// Collect variables defined by an assignment LHS.
847: ///
848: /// For simple `identifier` LHS, adds the name to `assigned`.
849: /// For `multioutput_variable`, adds each identifier.
850: /// For indexed assignment (`function_call` or `field_expression`), checks
851: /// the expression for uses but does NOT add new variables (the base
852: /// variable must already exist).
853: fn collect_assignment_targets(
854:     lhs: Node,
855:     source: &str,
856:     assigned: &mut HashSet<String>,
857:     uses: &mut Vec<PossiblyUnsetVar>,
858: ) {
859:     match lhs.kind() {
860:         "identifier" => {
861:             assigned.insert(node_text(lhs, source).to_string());
862:         }
863:         "multioutput_variable" => {
864:             let mut cursor = lhs.walk();
865:             for child in lhs.children(&mut cursor) {
866:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
867:                     assigned.insert(node_text(child, source).to_string());
868:                 }
869:             }
870:         }
871:         "function_call" | "field_expression" | "cell_index" => {
872:             // Indexed assignment: `A(i) = ...` or `obj.field = ...`
873:             // The base variable is a use, not a new definition.
874:             collect_uses_in_expr(lhs, source, assigned, uses);
875:         }
876:         _ => {
877:             collect_uses_in_expr(lhs, source, assigned, uses);
878:         }
879:     }
880: }

886: /// Compute the intersection of multiple `HashSet<String>` collections.
887: ///
888: /// Returns the set of strings present in ALL input sets.
889: fn intersect_sets(sets: &[HashSet<String>]) -> HashSet<String> {
890:     if sets.is_empty() {
891:         return HashSet::new();
892:     }
893:     let mut result = sets[0].clone();
894:     for set in &sets[1..] {
895:         result.retain(|name| set.contains(name));
896:     }
897:     result
898: }

1: //! # FORMATTING_ENGINE: Formatting Suggestion Checks
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "FORMATTING_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Formatting Suggestion Checks"
6: //! category = "formatting"
7: //! severity = "info"
8: //! fix = true
9: //! icon = "lucide/align-left"
10: //! slug = "formatting"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Suggests formatting improvements for MATLAB code. All 7 checks share a
16: //! single `FormattingEngine` that runs as a file-level rule, walking the whole
17: //! tree once and applying every enabled check per node. Each diagnostic
18: //! carries the specific check ID (e.g. `NOCOMMA`, `NO4LP`). Individual checks
19: //! can be enabled, disabled, or reconfigured through their own
20: //! `[lint.rules.*]` tables.
21: //!
22: //! ## Check IDs
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
25: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: //! | NOCOMMA | info | yes | Extra comma is unnecessary. |
27: //! | NO4LP | info | yes | Parentheses are not needed in a FOR statement. |
28: //! | ALIGN | info | yes | This keyword might not be aligned with its matching END on line VAR_NUMBER. |
29: //! | NOPTS | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the statement to hide the output (in a script). |
30: //! | NOPRT | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the statement to hide the output (in a function). |
31: //! | PRTCAL | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the function call to hide the output. |
32: //! | NCOMMA | info | yes | Best practice is to separate output variables with commas. |
33: //!
34: //! ## Fix
35: //!
36: //! Each check rewrites the flagged construct directly:
37: //!
38: //! - NOCOMMA inserts a comma between space-separated row elements (`[1 2 3]` → `[1, 2, 3]`).
39: //! - NCOMMA inserts a comma between space-separated function arguments.
40: //! - NO4LP rewrites the indentation prefix of misindented statements.
41: //! - ALIGN re-indents `elseif`/`else` clauses to the column of their `if`.
42: //! - NOPTS and NOPRT strip unnecessary parentheses (`(x)` → `x`).
43: //! - PRTCAL rewrites a string-only call to command syntax (`disp('hello')` → `disp hello`).
44: //!
45: //! ## Examples
46: //!
47: //! ### Incorrect
48: //!
49: //! ```matlab
50: //! x = [1 2 3];
51: //! y = (a);
52: //! if (x > 0)
53: //!     disp('hello');
54: //! end
55: //! ```
56: //!
57: //! ### Correct
58: //!
59: //! ```matlab
60: //! x = [1, 2, 3];
61: //! y = a;
62: //! if x > 0
63: //!     disp hello;
64: //! end
65: //! ```
66: //!
67: //! ### Fixed
68: //!
69: //! ```diff
70: //! - x = [1 2 3];
71: //! + x = [1, 2, 3];
72: //! - y = (a);
73: //! + y = a;
74: //! - if (x > 0)
75: //! + if x > 0
76: //! ```

10:         &self,
11:         node: Node,
12:         source: &str,
13:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
14:     ) {
15:         let child_count = node.child_count();
16:         for i in 0..child_count {

18:                 continue;
19:             };

27:     fn check_row_commas(&self, row: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
28:         // Collect expression children (skip punctuation like "[", "]", ",", ";").
29:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
30:         let child_count = row.child_count();
31: 
32:         for i in 0..child_count {
33:             let Some(child) = row.child(i) else {
34:                 continue;
35:             };

37:

39:             // is inserted by the grammar when an element separator is missing.

41:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
42:                     let pos = child.start_position();

11:     /// arguments, suggest command syntax instead. For example:
12:     /// `disp('hello')` could be `disp hello`.

14:         // Only fire at statement level.

16:             .parent()

18:             .unwrap_or(false);
19:         if !is_statement_level {
20:             return;
21:         }

23:         // Must have an arguments node with only string/identifier children.
24:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
25:             return;
26:         };
27: 
28:         let mut arg_texts = Vec::new();
29:         let mut all_strings = true;
30:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
31:         let mut expr_count = 0;
32: 
33:         for i in 0..arg_count {
34:             let Some(arg) = args_node.child(i) else {
35:                 continue;
36:             };
37:             let kind = arg.kind();
38:             // Skip punctuation (parens, commas).
39:             if is_punctuation(kind) || kind == "," {
40:                 continue;
41:             }
42:             expr_count += 1;
43:             if kind == "string" {
44:                 // Extract string content without quotes.
45:                 let text = &source[arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte()];

48:                     .trim_end_matches('\'')

52:                 if unquoted.contains(' ') || unquoted.contains('\'') {

2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "NOSEMI"
5: //! title = "Trailing Semicolon Missing"

9: //! icon = "lucide/code"

12: //! ## Rule
13: //!
14: //! Flags MATLAB statements that produce output without a trailing semicolon.
15: //! In MATLAB, such statements print their result to the console, which is
16: //! almost always unintentional in production code and can cause significant
17: //! performance degradation in loops.
18: //!
19: //! ## Fix
20: //!
21: //! Inserts a trailing semicolon immediately after the statement, suppressing
22: //! the console output without changing program behavior.
23: //!
24: //! ## Examples

28: //! ```matlab
29: //! x = compute_value()

31: //! ```

38: //! ```

200: /// Determine whether a statement node is followed by a semicolon.

206: fn has_trailing_semicolon(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
207:     // Strategy 1: Check next named/unnamed siblings for ";"
208:     let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
209:     while let Some(sib) = sibling {
210:         let kind = sib.kind();

216:         // If the next meaningful sibling is ";", the statement is terminated.
217:         if kind == ";" {
218:             return true;
219:         }

221:         break;
222:     }

226:     let after = &source[node.end_byte()..];

233:             ' ' | '\t' => continue,
234:             // Any other character means something else follows.
235:             _ => return false,
236:         }
237:     }

All changes are complete and verified. Here's the summary.

## Reimplemented checks

**`unused/` (Unused Constructions)**
- `MANU` — now flags an unused **method input argument** (was "method never called").
- `NUSED` — new `check_nused.rs`; flags an unused **global or persistent** variable (was "input argument unused").
- `PUSE` — now flags only **persistent** variables (was flagging global+persistent with the PUSE message).
- `SETNU` — now flags an assignment whose value is **never subsequently used** (dead store before reassignment); removed the "only fire when NASGU disabled" hack.
- `UNRCH` — verified return/break/continue work; added `error(...)`-call termination detection with byte-range dedup.
- `EQEFF` — now fires only on `==` (was firing on any comparison operator like `<`, `~=`, etc.).
- `VANUS` — now flags an unused **`varargin`** input argument (was "value assigned to `ans` unused").
- `DEFNU` — left unchanged (already correctly flags an unused local *function*).

**`custom_checks.rs`**
- `SYSBANG` — removed the dead `system_command` branch (a non-existent node type with a non-verbatim message); kept the correct `!`-prefixed `command` detection.

**`codegen/`**
- `EMSCR` — reimplemented script detection to exclude `function_definition` **and `class_definition`** files (was flagging classdef files as scripts); removed orphaned `has_child_of_kind`.

**`formatting/`**
- `NOCOMMA` — now flags a **trailing/extra comma** (was "use commas to separate elements").
- `NCOMMA` — now flags **space-separated output variables** (`[a b] = f()`) on `multioutput_variable` (was "comma to separate input args").
- `NOPTS` — now flags an assignment in a **script** without a trailing semicolon (was "unnecessary parentheses").
- `NOPRT` — now flags an assignment in a **function** without a trailing semicolon (was "unnecessary parentheses").
- `PRTCAL` — now flags a **bare function call statement** without a trailing semicolon (was "consider command syntax").

Orphaned helpers deleted: `find_arguments_child`, `inner_paren_text`, `find_inner_expr` (formatting), `has_child_of_kind` (codegen).

## Caveats / not fully confident

- **SETNU vs NASGU boundary is fuzzy.** I implemented "value never subsequently used" (a dead store overwritten before any read). The exact MathWorks split between NASGU and SETNU isn't documented precisely, so simple unused assignments now fire both NASGU and SETNU.
- **NUSED/PUSE overlap.** Per the verbatim messages, NUSED covers "global or persistent" and PUSE covers "persistent", so an unused `persistent` fires both. This follows the message text literally but is redundant.
- **MANU vs INUSD/INUSA overlap.** `check_unused_inputs` still fires INUSD/INUSA on method scopes (not in my task scope), so a method with an unused input now also gets those IDs alongside MANU.

Verification: `cargo build -p mlt_rules` (no errors), `cargo test -p mlt_rules` (1461 passed), `cargo clippy -p mlt_rules` (zero warnings), full `cargo build` clean.

One note: I did not update the `//!` docstring `## Fix`/`## Examples` prose in `formatting/mod.rs` and `unused/mod.rs` (still describes old behavior), since the task scoped me to detection logic only. Those docs will need regeneration if you want them to reflect the new semantics.
